findings.detail: The long devotes much of its ending to enumerating details not established, whether the board resumed, and what further facts are needed to substantiate effects. That source-gap inventory overwhelms the factual context of the announced pause and stated rationale.

The medium repeats the headline and generic standalone-event/downstream-effects template without identifying any of the specific policies, setbacks or reactions described in the long. The long supplies a concrete account, but the medium is not a reader-facing summary.
The medium repeats the title and the source’s two-sentence abstract, then appends generic standalone-event/downstream-effects language.

The long is only a brief, general statement that a New York Times report described a shift affecting lawful immigrants. It names no policies, affected groups, dates, or consequences, so it does not meaningfully expand on the medium.

The long reproduces the opinion headline and article excerpt verbatim, including “Continue reading...,” then appends the generic catalog rationale and claims not to infer unstated effects. This is source-excerpt/template content rather than a reader-facing summary of the commentary.

The medium repeats the article headline and subhead verbatim, then appends generic standalone-event/downstream-effects claims. The long supplies the actual account of the reported pause and its limits.

The medium consists of the title and headline subhead followed by generic standalone-event/downstream-effects language. It does not summarize the wedding decision or Trump’s stated reason; the long adds the report details.

The long repeats the supplied context’s sweeping conclusion that Trump’s rhetoric incited violence, caused death threats, justified crackdowns by dictators and constituted an assault on democracy as established fact. The medium gives narrower evidence—reported threats and a warning that the rhetoric could lead to violence. The long converts a warning and individual reports into broad causal conclusions without support in the medium or specific evidence here.

The medium repeats the headline and subhead and appends generic standalone-event/downstream-effects text without explaining the Senate vote or funding dispute. The long gives a specific account of the failed bill and objections.
